es.B: Emborracharé a sus jefes y a sus sabios, a sus gobernadores, a sus delegados y a sus guerreros, \q y dormirán un sueño que dure para siempre y nunca despertarán, \q afirma el Rey, \q cuyo nombre es {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos.
es.R: Emborracharé a sus dirigentes y a sus sabios, a sus gobernadores, a sus funcionarios y a sus soldados. \q Luego se dormirán para siempre y nunca despertarán, \q dice el Rey, \q cuyo nombre es {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos.

fr.L: Et j’enivrerai ses princes et ses sages, ses gouverneurs et ses magistrats et ses guerriers, \q et ils dormiront d’un sommeil éternel et ne se réveilleront pas, \q déclare le Roi, \q dont le nom [est] {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées.
fr.B: J’enivrerai ses chefs et ses sages, ses gouverneurs, ses magistrats et ses guerriers, \q et ils dormiront d’un sommeil sans fin et ne se réveilleront jamais, \q déclare le Roi, \q dont le nom est {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées.
fr.R: J’enivrerai ses chefs et ses sages, ses gouverneurs, ses magistrats et ses soldats. \q Puis ils s’endormiront pour toujours et ne se réveilleront jamais, \q dit le Roi, \q dont le nom est {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées.

sw.L: Nami nitawalevya wakuu wake na wenye hekima wake, maliwali wake na maafisa wake na mashujaa wake, \q nao watalala usingizi wa milele wasiamke, \q asema Mfalme, \q ambaye jina {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}} [ni] {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi.
sw.B: Nitawalevya maafisa wake na wenye hekima wake, maliwali wake, manaibu wake na mashujaa wake, \q nao watalala usingizi wa milele wasiamke kamwe, \q asema Mfalme, \q ambaye jina {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}} ni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi.
sw.R: Nitawalevya viongozi wake na wenye hekima wake, maliwali wake, maafisa wake na askari wake. \q Kisha watalala usingizi milele wala hawataamka kamwe, \q anasema Mfalme, \q ambaye jina {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}} ni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi.

vi.L: Ta sẽ làm cho các quan trưởng, các người khôn ngoan, các tổng đốc, các quan chức và các dũng sĩ của nó say sưa, \q và chúng sẽ ngủ một giấc ngủ đời đời và không thức dậy, \q Vua phán vậy, \q danh {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} [là] {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân.
vi.B: Ta sẽ làm cho các quan chức và các người khôn ngoan của nó say, cả các tổng đốc, các phó quan và các dũng sĩ của nó, \q và chúng sẽ ngủ một giấc ngủ kéo dài mãi mãi và không bao giờ thức dậy, \q Vua phán vậy, \q là Đấng có danh là {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân.
vi.R: Ta sẽ làm cho các nhà lãnh đạo và các người khôn ngoan của nó say, cả các tổng đốc, các quan chức và quân lính của nó. \q Rồi chúng sẽ ngủ mãi mãi và không bao giờ thức dậy nữa, \q Vua phán, \q là Đấng có danh là {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân.

ko.L: 그리고 내가 그의 고관들과 그의 지혜자들과 그의 총독들과 그의 관리들과 그의 용사들을 취하게 하리니, \q 그들이 영원한 잠을 자고 깨어나지 못할 것이다. \q 왕의 선언이다. \q 그의 이름은 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}다.
ko.B: 내가 그의 관리들과 지혜자들과 총독들과 부관들과 용사들을 취하게 하리니, \q 그들이 영원한 잠에 빠져 다시는 깨어나지 못할 것이다. \q 왕이 말한다. \q 그의 이름은 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}다.
ko.R: 나는 바빌론의 지도자들과 지혜로운 사람들과 총독들과 관리들과 군인들을 취하게 하겠다. \q 그러면 그들은 영원히 잠들어 다시는 깨어나지 못할 것이다. \q 왕이 말한다. \q 그 왕의 이름은 하늘의 군대를 거느린 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}다.

pt.L: E embriagarei os seus príncipes e os seus sábios, os seus governadores, e os seus oficiais, e os seus guerreiros, \q e dormirão um sono perpétuo e não acordarão, \q declara o Rei, \q cujo nome [é] {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos.
pt.B: Embriagarei os seus oficiais e os seus sábios, os seus governadores, os seus intendentes e os seus guerreiros, \q e dormirão um sono que dura para sempre e nunca mais acordarão, \q declara o Rei, \q cujo nome é {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos.
pt.R: Vou deixar bêbados os seus líderes e os seus sábios, os seus governadores, oficiais e soldados. \q Depois eles vão cair num sono para sempre e nunca mais vão acordar, \q diz o Rei, \q cujo nome é {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos.

am.L: አለቆቿንና ጠቢባኖቿን፣ አገረ ገዦቿንና ሹማምንቷን ኃያላኖቿንም አሰክራቸዋለሁ፤ \q የዘላለምም እንቅልፍ ይተኛሉ፤ አይነቁምም፣ \q ይላል ንጉሡ፣ \q ስሙ {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ጸባኦት የሆነው።
am.B: ሹማምንቷንና ጠቢባኖቿን፣ አገረ ገዦቿን፣ ምክትሎቿንና ጦረኞቿን አሰክራቸዋለሁ፤ \q ለዘላለም የሚቆይ እንቅልፍ ይተኛሉ፤ ፈጽሞም አይነቁም፣ \q ይላል ንጉሡ፣ \q ስሙ የሠራዊት አምላክ {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} የሆነው።
am.R: መሪዎቿንና ጠቢባኖቿን፣ አገረ ገዦቿን፣ ባለ ሥልጣናቷንና ወታደሮቿን አሰክራቸዋለሁ። \q ከዚያም ለዘላለም ያንቀላፋሉ፤ ፈጽሞም አይነቁም፣ \q ይላል ንጉሡ፣ \q ስሙ የሠራዊት አምላክ {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} የሆነው።

hi.L: और मैं उसके हाकिमों और उसके बुद्धिमानों को, उसके राज्यपालों और उसके अधिकारियों और उसके वीर योद्धाओं को मतवाला कर दूँगा, \q और वे सदा की नींद सोएँगे और न जागेंगे, \q उस राजा की यह वाणी है, \q जिनका नाम सेनाओं के {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} [है]।
hi.B: मैं उसके अधिकारियों और बुद्धिमानों को, उसके राज्यपालों, उप-अधिकारियों और वीर योद्धाओं को मतवाला कर दूँगा, \q और वे ऐसी नींद सोएँगे जो सदा बनी रहे और कभी न जागेंगे, \q उस राजा की यह वाणी है, \q जिनका नाम सेनाओं के {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} है।
hi.R: मैं उसके अगुवों और बुद्धिमानों को, और उसके राज्यपालों, अधिकारियों और सैनिकों को मतवाला कर दूँगा। \q फिर वे सदा के लिए सो जाएँगे और कभी नहीं जागेंगे, \q उस राजा का यह कहना है, \q जिनका नाम सेनाओं के {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} है।

ru.L: И опьяню {{deity_pronoun:я|Я}} его князей и его мудрецов, его наместников, и его начальников, и его воинов-богатырей, \q и уснут они вечным сном и не проснутся, \q — слово Царя, \q {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Яхве}} Саваоф — {{deity_pronoun:его|Его}} имя.
ru.B: Я опьяню его вельмож и мудрецов, его наместников, начальников и воинов, \q и они уснут сном, который длится вечно, и никогда не проснутся, \q — говорит Царь, \q чьё имя — {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Яхве}} Саваоф.
ru.R: Я опьяню его начальников и мудрецов, его правителей, чиновников и воинов. \q Потом они уснут навсегда и больше никогда не проснутся, \q — говорит Царь, \q чьё имя — {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Яхве}} Воинств.

ja.L: わたしは、その長たちとその知者たち、その総督たちとその長官たちとその勇士たちを酔わせる。 \q 彼らは永遠の眠りに就き、目を覚まさない―― \q 王の言葉―― \q その名は万軍の{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}。
ja.B: わたしは、その高官たちと知者たち、総督たちと長官たちと勇士たちを酔わせる。 \q 彼らは永遠に続く眠りに就き、二度と目を覚まさない、 \q と王は告げる。 \q その名は万軍の{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}。
ja.R: わたしは、その指導者たちと知恵ある者たち、総督や役人たちや兵士たちを酔わせる。 \q そして彼らは眠り込み、永遠に目を覚まさない、 \q と王は言う。 \q その名は、天の軍勢を率いる{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}。

decisions.choice: make drunk ... sleep a perpetual sleep: the words of verse 39 return
decisions.reason: The feast of verse 39 is now given to Babylon's leaders. All the ranks of her rulers drink the LORD's cup and die. The words are those of verse 39.

decisions.choice: the King, whose name is the LORD of hosts: the true king above the king of Babylon
decisions.reason: The title answers the "king of Babylon" (verses 31, 34). The LORD is the King of all the earth (10:7, 10; 46:18; 48:15).

decisions.choice: princes, governors, officials: the ranks of the empire's rulers
decisions.reason: As in verse 23, governors and officials are titles of the empire's provincial rulers; princes are the court's leading men.

decisions.choice: princes (L), officials (B), leaders (R); her officials (L), deputies (B), officials (R)
decisions.reason: *Sar* follows the settled wording: "princes", "officials", "leaders". Since Balanced already uses "officials" for *sar*, it says "deputies" for the second title, which is "officials" in verse 23. The words about sleep keep the wording of verse 39 at each level.

decisions.choice: the Portuguese of verse 39; os seus oficiais (L), intendentes (B)
decisions.reason: The sleep of verse 39 returns (m1) in its words at each level. Sar keeps "príncipes / oficiais / líderes", so Balanced says "intendentes" for the lower officials, as the English says "deputies".

decisions.choice: sar "हाकिम" (L), "अधिकारी" (B), "अगुवे" (R); seganim "अधिकारी" (L, R), "उप-अधिकारी" (B)
decisions.reason: Sar keeps Jeremiah's wording at each level; since Balanced already uses "अधिकारी" for sar, it says "उप-अधिकारी" (deputies) for the second title, as the English Balanced does.

decisions.choice: "उस राजा की यह वाणी है" (L, B); "उस राजा का यह कहना है" (R)
decisions.reason: Neum with "the King" in place of the divine name keeps the formula's form at each level, and the honorific "जिनका" shows that the King is God.

decisions.choice: князья, наместники, начальники (L); вельможи, наместники, начальники (B); начальники, правители, чиновники (R)
decisions.reason: Sar keeps the three forms set for it (L, B, R); since Readable already uses "начальники" for sar, it says "чиновники" for the second title.

decisions.choice: the wording of verse 39
decisions.reason: The same sleep of death as verse 39, in its wording at each level.

decisions.choice: ne'um hammelekh YHWH tseva'ot shemo in the words of JER 48:15 ("――王の言葉―― その名は万軍の{D}。" L; "と王は告げる。その名は…" B; "と王は言う。" R); the sleep line as 51:39.
decisions.reason: m2: the same formula as 46:18 and 48:15.

source.text: כֹּֽה־אָמַ֞ר יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֗וֹת חֹ֠מוֹת בָּבֶ֤ל הָֽרְחָבָה֙ עַרְעֵ֣ר תִּתְעַרְעָ֔ר וּשְׁעָרֶ֥יהָ הַגְּבֹהִ֖ים בָּאֵ֣שׁ יִצַּ֑תּוּ וְיִֽגְע֨וּ עַמִּ֧ים בְּדֵי־רִ֛יק וּלְאֻמִּ֥ים בְּדֵי־אֵ֖שׁ וְיָעֵֽפוּ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: Thus says Yahweh of hosts: [The] walls of Babylon, the broad, utterly will be laid bare, and her gates, the high, with fire will be burned; and toil peoples for nothing, and nations for fire, and they grow weary.

en.L: Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts: The broad wall of Babylon will be utterly laid bare, \q and her high gates will be burned with fire; \q and peoples toil for nothing, and nations for fire, and they grow weary.
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says this: The broad wall of Babylon will be leveled to the ground, \q and her high gates will be set on fire. \q The peoples toil for nothing; the nations wear themselves out only for the fire.
en.R: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says: Babylon's thick walls will be completely torn down. \q Her tall gates will be burned. \q The people of the nations worked hard to build them, but it was all for nothing. They wore themselves out, only for it all to burn.

es.L: Así dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los ejércitos: El ancho muro de Babilonia será derribado por completo, \q y sus altas puertas serán quemadas con fuego; \q y los pueblos trabajan para nada, y las naciones para el fuego, y se cansan.
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos dice esto: El ancho muro de Babilonia será arrasado hasta el suelo, \q y sus altas puertas serán incendiadas. \q Los pueblos se fatigan para nada; las naciones se agotan solo para el fuego.
es.R: Esto es lo que dice {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} de los Ejércitos: Las gruesas murallas de Babilonia serán derribadas por completo. \q Sus altas puertas serán quemadas. \q La gente de las naciones trabajó mucho para construirlas, pero todo fue en vano. Se agotaron para que todo terminara quemado.

fr.L: Ainsi parle {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées : La large muraille de Babylone sera entièrement rasée, \q et ses hautes portes seront brûlées par le feu ; \q et les peuples se fatiguent pour le néant, et les nations pour le feu, et ils s’épuisent.
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées dit ceci : La large muraille de Babylone sera rasée jusqu’au sol, \q et ses hautes portes seront livrées au feu. \q Les peuples se fatiguent pour rien ; les nations s’épuisent seulement pour le feu.
fr.R: Voici ce que dit {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} des armées : Les épaisses murailles de Babylone seront complètement démolies. \q Ses hautes portes seront brûlées. \q Les gens des nations ont travaillé dur pour les construire, mais tout cela n’a servi à rien. Ils se sont épuisés, et tout va brûler.

sw.L: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi asema hivi: Ukuta mpana wa Babeli utabomolewa kabisa, \q na malango yake marefu yatateketezwa kwa moto; \q na mataifa wanajitaabisha bure, na mataifa kwa ajili ya moto, nao wanachoka.
sw.B: Hivi ndivyo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi asemavyo: Ukuta mpana wa Babeli utabomolewa mpaka chini, \q na malango yake marefu yatachomwa moto. \q Mataifa wanajitaabisha bure; mataifa wanajichosha kwa ajili ya moto tu.
sw.R: Hili ndilo {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} wa majeshi analosema: Kuta nene za Babeli zitabomolewa kabisa. \q Malango yake marefu yatachomwa moto. \q Watu wa mataifa walifanya kazi kwa bidii kuyajenga, lakini yote yalikuwa bure. Walijichosha, ili tu yote yaungue.

vi.L: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán thế này: Tường thành rộng lớn của Ba-by-lôn sẽ bị san bằng hoàn toàn, \q các cổng cao của nó sẽ bị lửa đốt; \q các dân lao khổ cho điều hư không, các nước nhọc nhằn cho lửa, và chúng mệt mỏi.
vi.B: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán như vầy: Tường thành rộng lớn của Ba-by-lôn sẽ bị san bằng, \q các cổng cao của nó sẽ bị phóng hỏa. \q Các dân lao nhọc vô ích; các nước kiệt sức chỉ để cho lửa thiêu.
vi.R: Đây là lời {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} Vạn Quân phán: Tường thành dày của Ba-by-lôn sẽ bị phá đổ hoàn toàn. \q Các cổng cao của nó sẽ bị đốt cháy. \q Dân các nước đã ra sức xây dựng chúng, nhưng tất cả đều vô ích. Họ đã kiệt sức, chỉ để mọi thứ bị thiêu rụi.

ko.L: 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이와 같이 말씀하신다. 바빌론의 넓은 성벽은 완전히 헐리고, \q 그의 높은 성문들은 불에 탈 것이다. \q 민족들이 헛되이 수고하고, 나라들이 불을 위하여 [수고하다가] 지칠 것이다.
ko.B: 만군의 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 이렇게 말씀하신다. 바빌론의 넓은 성벽은 땅바닥까지 허물어지고, \q 그 높은 성문들은 불타 버릴 것이다. \q 민족들의 수고가 헛되고, 나라들이 애써 지은 것이 불에 타 버리니 그들이 지칠 뿐이다.
ko.R: 하늘의 군대를 거느리신 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 하시는 말씀이다. 바빌론의 두꺼운 성벽은 완전히 허물어질 것이다. \q 그 높은 성문들은 불타 버릴 것이다. \q 여러 나라 사람들이 그것을 쌓으려고 애썼지만 모두 헛수고였다. 그들은 지치도록 일했지만 결국 다 불에 타 버릴 것이다.

pt.L: Assim diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos: O largo muro da Babilônia será totalmente arrasado, \q e as suas altas portas serão queimadas a fogo; \q e os povos se cansam por nada, e as nações para o fogo, e se fatigam.
pt.B: Assim diz {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos: O largo muro da Babilônia será arrasado até o chão, \q e as suas altas portas serão incendiadas. \q Os povos trabalham por nada; as nações se esgotam só para o fogo.
pt.R: É isto que {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} dos Exércitos diz: Os muros grossos da Babilônia vão ser derrubados por completo. \q As suas portas altas vão ser queimadas. \q As pessoas das nações trabalharam muito para construí-los, mas foi tudo para nada. Elas se esgotaram, só para tudo acabar queimado.

am.L: {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} ጸባኦት እንዲህ ይላል፦ ሰፊው የባቢሎን ቅጥር ፈጽሞ ይራቆታል፤ \q ረጃጅሞቹ በሮቿም በእሳት ይቃጠላሉ፤ \q ሕዝቦችም ለከንቱ፣ ወገኖችም ለእሳት ይደክማሉ፤ ይዝላሉም።
am.B: የሠራዊት አምላክ {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} እንዲህ ይላል፦ ሰፊው የባቢሎን ቅጥር ከመሬት ጋር ይደለደላል፤ \q ረጃጅሞቹ በሮቿም በእሳት ይቃጠላሉ። \q ሕዝቦች ለከንቱ ይደክማሉ፤ ወገኖችም ለእሳት ብቻ ይዝላሉ።
am.R: የሠራዊት አምላክ {{divine_name:እግዚአብሔር|ያህዌ}} እንዲህ ይላል፦ የባቢሎን ወፋፍራም ቅጥሮች ሙሉ በሙሉ ይፈርሳሉ። \q ረጃጅሞቹ በሮቿም ይቃጠላሉ። \q የሕዝቦች ሰዎች እነርሱን ለመሥራት ብዙ ደከሙ፤ ነገር ግን ሁሉም ከንቱ ሆነ። ደክመው የሠሩት ሁሉ ለእሳት ሆነ።

hi.L: सेनाओं के {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} यों कहते हैं: बाबुल की चौड़ी शहरपनाह पूरी तरह उघाड़ दी जाएगी, \q और उसके ऊँचे फाटक आग से जला दिए जाएँगे; \q और देशों के लोग व्यर्थ परिश्रम करते हैं, और जातियाँ आग के लिए, और वे थक जाते हैं।
hi.B: सेनाओं के {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} यह कहते हैं: बाबुल की चौड़ी शहरपनाह ढाकर भूमि में मिला दी जाएगी, \q और उसके ऊँचे फाटकों में आग लगा दी जाएगी। \q लोग व्यर्थ परिश्रम करते हैं; देश केवल आग के लिए अपने को थका डालते हैं।
hi.R: सेनाओं के {{divine_name:प्रभु|याहवे}} यह कहते हैं: बाबुल की मोटी दीवारें पूरी तरह ढा दी जाएँगी। \q उसके ऊँचे फाटक जला दिए जाएँगे। \q देशों के लोगों ने उन्हें बनाने के लिए कड़ी मेहनत की, पर सब व्यर्थ हुआ। वे थककर चूर हो गए, और अंत में सब कुछ जल गया।

ru.L: Так говорит {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Яхве}} Саваоф: Широкая стена Вавилона будет совершенно обнажена, \q и его высокие ворота будут сожжены огнём; \q и трудятся народы впустую, и племена — для огня, и изнемогают.
ru.B: Так говорит {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Яхве}} Саваоф: Широкая стена Вавилона будет сровнена с землёй, \q и его высокие ворота будут преданы огню. \q Народы трудятся впустую; племена изнуряют себя только для огня.
ru.R: Вот что говорит {{divine_name:ГОСПОДЬ|Яхве}} Воинств: Толстые стены Вавилона будут полностью разрушены. \q Его высокие ворота сгорят. \q Люди разных народов тяжело трудились, чтобы построить их, но всё было напрасно. Они изнуряли себя только для того, чтобы всё сгорело.

ja.L: 万軍の{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}はこう言われる。バビロンの広い城壁は、すっかり裸にされ、 \q その高い門は火で焼かれる。 \q もろもろの民は空しいことのために労苦し、国々は火のために[労苦し]、疲れ果てる。
ja.B: 万軍の{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}はこう言われる。バビロンの広い城壁は、地面まで崩され、 \q その高い門は火をつけられる。 \q もろもろの民は空しいことのために労苦し、国々は、ただ火に焼かれるもののために疲れ果てる。
ja.R: 天の軍勢を率いる{{divine_name:主|ヤハウェ}}はこう言われる。バビロンの厚い城壁は、すっかり取り壊される。 \q その高い門は焼かれる。 \q 国々の人々は、それを建てるために苦労したが、すべてむだだった。彼らは疲れ果てたが、それはみな焼かれてしまうだけだった。

decisions.choice: the broad wall ... utterly laid bare: Babylon's great walls razed to their foundations
decisions.reason: The noun is plural, "walls", for the whole system of walls, with a singular adjective "broad". Babylon's double walls were famous for their width. The doubled verb means to strip to the ground, to raze completely.

decisions.choice: peoples toil for nothing, nations for fire: the same saying as Habakkuk 2:13
decisions.reason: Habakkuk 2:13 has almost the same words in the reverse order: "peoples toil for fire, and nations weary themselves for nothing". It is a saying about empires built by forced labor: all their work ends in flames. Habakkuk has not yet been translated in this project; when it is, the two should be compared. The last verb, "and they grow weary", returns at the end of verse 64.

decisions.choice: for nothing: for the sake of emptiness
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "for enough of emptiness", that is, their labor gains them nothing but emptiness, and "enough of fire", only enough to feed the flames.

decisions.choice: utterly laid bare (L); leveled to the ground (B); completely torn down (R); wear themselves out only for the fire (B, R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the doubled verb means (m1) and make the last line clear. Readable adds that the peoples built the walls, which the saying implies.

decisions.choice: y se cansan (L)
decisions.reason: The last words, "and they will grow weary", return in verse 64; they echo Habakkuk 2:13.

decisions.choice: peoples (ʿammim) and nations (leʾummim) side by side are "ሕዝቦች" and "ወገኖች", as the Psalms list.
decisions.reason: Two words for two Hebrew words in one line. Habakkuk 2:13 has the same saying and should match when drafted.
Literal keeps two words for the two Hebrew words (ammim, leummim); the saying is the one found in Habakkuk 2:13, which is to share this wording.

decisions.choice: народы ... племена
decisions.reason: The poetry note's pair for "peoples" and "nations"; the saying is the same as Habakkuk 2:13 (m2), which should share this wording.

decisions.choice: The saying in the words of HAB 2:13 (もろもろの民…労苦し / 国々は空しいことのために疲れ果てる / ただ火に焼かれるもののために), in Jeremiah's order (riq first, then 'esh).
decisions.reason: m2: the same saying as Habakkuk; the pair is reversed in the Hebrew.

source.text: הַדָּבָ֞ר אֲשֶׁר־צִוָּ֣ה׀יִרְמְיָ֣הוּ הַנָּבִ֗יא אֶת־שְׂרָיָ֣ה בֶן־נֵרִיָּה֮ בֶּן־מַחְסֵיָה֒ בְּלֶכְתּ֞וֹ אֶת־צִדְקִיָּ֤הוּ מֶֽלֶךְ־יְהוּדָה֙ בָּבֶ֔ל בִּשְׁנַ֥ת הָרְבִעִ֖ית לְמָלְכ֑וֹ וּשְׂרָיָ֖ה שַׂ֥ר מְנוּחָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: The word that commanded Jeremiah the prophet Seraiah son of Neriah son of Mahseiah in his going with Zedekiah king of Judah [to] Babylon in the fourth year of his reigning; and Seraiah [was] officer of [the] resting place.

en.L: The word that Jeremiah the prophet commanded Seraiah son of Neriah, son of Mahseiah, when he went with Zedekiah king of Judah to Babylon in the fourth year of his reign. Now Seraiah [was] officer of the resting place.
en.B: This is the message that Jeremiah the prophet gave as a command to Seraiah son of Neriah, son of Mahseiah, when he went to Babylon with Zedekiah king of Judah in the fourth year of his reign. Seraiah was the quartermaster.
en.R: This is the message that Jeremiah the prophet gave to Seraiah son of Neriah and grandson of Mahseiah. Seraiah was going to Babylon with Zedekiah king of Judah. This was in Zedekiah's fourth year as king. Seraiah was the officer in charge of the places where the king stopped to rest on the journey.

es.L: La palabra que Jeremías el profeta mandó a Seraías hijo de Nerías, hijo de Maasías, cuando fue con Sedequías, rey de Judá, a Babilonia en el año cuarto de su reinado. Y Seraías [era] jefe del lugar de descanso.
es.B: Este es el mensaje que el profeta Jeremías le dio como orden a Seraías hijo de Nerías, hijo de Maasías, cuando fue a Babilonia con Sedequías, rey de Judá, en el cuarto año de su reinado. Seraías era el jefe de alojamiento.
es.R: Este es el mensaje que el profeta Jeremías le dio a Seraías, hijo de Nerías y nieto de Maasías. Seraías iba a Babilonia con Sedequías, rey de Judá. Era el cuarto año del reinado de Sedequías. Seraías era el oficial encargado de los lugares donde el rey se detenía a descansar durante el viaje.

fr.L: La parole que Jérémie le prophète commanda à Seraya fils de Nériya, fils de Mahséya, quand il alla avec Sédécias, roi de Juda, à Babylone, en la quatrième année de son règne. Or Seraya [était] chef des étapes.
fr.B: Voici l’ordre que le prophète Jérémie donna à Seraya fils de Nériya, fils de Mahséya, quand celui-ci se rendit à Babylone avec Sédécias, roi de Juda, la quatrième année de son règne. Seraya était le responsable des étapes.
fr.R: Voici le message que le prophète Jérémie a donné à Seraya, fils de Nériya et petit-fils de Mahséya. Seraya partait pour Babylone avec Sédécias, roi de Juda. C’était la quatrième année du règne de Sédécias. Seraya était l’officier chargé des endroits où le roi s’arrêtait pour se reposer pendant le voyage.

sw.L: Neno ambalo Yeremia nabii alimwagiza Seraya mwana wa Neria, mwana wa Maseya, alipokwenda pamoja na Sedekia mfalme wa Yuda hata Babeli katika mwaka wa nne wa kutawala kwake. Naye Seraya [alikuwa] afisa wa mahali pa kupumzika.
sw.B: Huu ndio ujumbe ambao nabii Yeremia alimpa kama agizo Seraya mwana wa Neria, mwana wa Maseya, alipokwenda Babeli pamoja na Sedekia mfalme wa Yuda katika mwaka wa nne wa utawala wake. Seraya alikuwa msimamizi wa makao ya safari.
sw.R: Huu ndio ujumbe ambao nabii Yeremia alimpa Seraya mwana wa Neria na mjukuu wa Maseya. Seraya alikuwa akienda Babeli pamoja na Sedekia mfalme wa Yuda. Hii ilikuwa katika mwaka wa nne wa utawala wa Sedekia. Seraya alikuwa afisa aliyesimamia mahali ambapo mfalme alisimama kupumzika safarini.

vi.L: Lời mà nhà tiên tri Giê-rê-mi đã truyền cho Sê-ra-gia con trai Nê-ri-gia, con trai Mách-sê-gia, khi ông cùng Sê-đê-kia vua Giu-đa đi đến Ba-by-lôn vào năm thứ tư đời trị vì của vua. Sê-ra-gia [là] quan coi việc nghỉ chân.
vi.B: Đây là sứ điệp nhà tiên tri Giê-rê-mi đã truyền cho Sê-ra-gia con trai Nê-ri-gia, con trai Mách-sê-gia, khi ông cùng Sê-đê-kia vua Giu-đa đi đến Ba-by-lôn vào năm thứ tư đời trị vì của vua. Sê-ra-gia là quan lo việc doanh trại.
vi.R: Đây là sứ điệp nhà tiên tri Giê-rê-mi đã ban cho Sê-ra-gia con trai Nê-ri-gia và cháu nội Mách-sê-gia. Sê-ra-gia sắp đi Ba-by-lôn cùng với Sê-đê-kia vua Giu-đa. Lúc ấy là năm thứ tư đời Sê-đê-kia làm vua. Sê-ra-gia là viên quan lo những nơi vua dừng chân nghỉ ngơi trên đường đi.

ko.L: 마세야의 손자 네리야의 아들 스라야가 유다 왕 시드기야와 함께 그의 통치 제4년에 바빌론으로 갈 때에 예언자 예레미야가 그에게 명령한 말씀이다. 스라야는 숙영 담당관이었다.
ko.B: 이것은 마세야의 손자요 네리야의 아들인 스라야가 유다 왕 시드기야가 다스린 지 4년째 되는 해에 시드기야와 함께 바빌론으로 갈 때, 예언자 예레미야가 그에게 명령한 말씀이다. 스라야는 왕의 숙영 담당관이었다.
ko.R: 이것은 예언자 예레미야가 네리야의 아들이며 마세야의 손자인 스라야에게 준 말씀이다. 스라야는 유다 왕 시드기야와 함께 바빌론으로 가는 길이었다. 그때는 시드기야가 왕이 된 지 4년째 되는 해였다. 스라야는 왕이 길을 가다가 쉬어 갈 곳을 마련하는 일을 맡은 관리였다.

pt.L: A palavra que Jeremias, o profeta, ordenou a Seraías, filho de Nerias, filho de Maaseias, quando ele foi com Zedequias, rei de Judá, para a Babilônia, no quarto ano do seu reinado. E Seraías [era] o chefe do acampamento.
pt.B: Esta é a mensagem que o profeta Jeremias deu como ordem a Seraías, filho de Nerias, filho de Maaseias, quando ele foi para a Babilônia com Zedequias, rei de Judá, no quarto ano do seu reinado. Seraías era o encarregado das paradas da viagem.
pt.R: Esta é a mensagem que o profeta Jeremias deu a Seraías, filho de Nerias e neto de Maaseias. Seraías ia para a Babilônia com Zedequias, rei de Judá. Isso foi no quarto ano em que Zedequias era rei. Seraías era o oficial encarregado dos lugares onde o rei parava para descansar na viagem.

am.L: ነቢዩ ኤርምያስ የመሕሤያ ልጅ የኔርያ ልጅ ሠራያን ያዘዘው ቃል፤ [ይህም ሠራያ] ከይሁዳ ንጉሥ ከሴዴቅያስ ጋር በንግሥናው በአራተኛው ዓመት ወደ ባቢሎን በሄደ ጊዜ [ነው]። ሠራያም የማረፊያው አለቃ ነበረ።
am.B: ነቢዩ ኤርምያስ የመሕሤያ ልጅ የኔርያ ልጅ ሠራያን ያዘዘው መልእክት ይህ ነው፤ ይህም ሠራያ በይሁዳ ንጉሥ በሴዴቅያስ የንግሥና ዘመን በአራተኛው ዓመት ከንጉሡ ጋር ወደ ባቢሎን በሄደ ጊዜ ነበር። ሠራያ የስንቅና የሰፈር ኃላፊ ነበር።
am.R: ነቢዩ ኤርምያስ ለኔርያ ልጅ፣ ለመሕሤያ የልጅ ልጅ ለሠራያ የሰጠው መልእክት ይህ ነው። ሠራያ ከይሁዳ ንጉሥ ከሴዴቅያስ ጋር ወደ ባቢሎን ይሄድ ነበር። ይህም ሴዴቅያስ በነገሠ በአራተኛው ዓመት ነበር። ሠራያ በጉዞው ላይ ንጉሡ የሚያርፍባቸውን ስፍራዎች የሚያዘጋጅ ባለ ሥልጣን ነበር።

hi.L: वह वचन जो यिर्मयाह भविष्यद्वक्ता ने महसेयाह के पोते, नेरिय्याह के पुत्र सरायाह को आज्ञा देकर कहा, जब वह यहूदा के राजा सिदकिय्याह के साथ उसके राज्य के चौथे वर्ष में बाबुल को गया। और सरायाह विश्राम-स्थान का अधिकारी [था]।
hi.B: यह वह संदेश है जो यिर्मयाह भविष्यद्वक्ता ने महसेयाह के पोते, नेरिय्याह के पुत्र सरायाह को आज्ञा के रूप में दिया, जब वह यहूदा के राजा सिदकिय्याह के राज्य के चौथे वर्ष में उसके साथ बाबुल को गया। सरायाह पड़ाव का प्रबंधक था।
hi.R: यह वह संदेश है जो यिर्मयाह नबी ने नेरिय्याह के बेटे और महसेयाह के पोते सरायाह को दिया। सरायाह यहूदा के राजा सिदकिय्याह के साथ बाबुल जा रहा था। यह सिदकिय्याह के राजा होने का चौथा वर्ष था। सरायाह उस अधिकारी का काम करता था जो यात्रा में राजा के रुकने और आराम करने के ठिकानों का प्रबंध करता था।

ru.L: Слово, которое повелел Иеремия пророк Сераии, сыну Нирии, сына Махсеи, когда тот шёл с Седекией, царём Иудейским, в Вавилон в четвёртый год его царствования. А Сераия [был] начальником стоянки.
ru.B: Вот слово, которое пророк Иеремия дал как повеление Сераии, сыну Нирии, сына Махсеи, когда тот отправлялся в Вавилон вместе с Седекией, царём Иуды, в четвёртый год его царствования. Сераия ведал стоянками в пути.
ru.R: Вот весть, которую пророк Иеремия передал Сераии, сыну Нирии и внуку Махсеи. Сераия отправлялся в Вавилон вместе с Седекией, царём Иуды. Это было в четвёртый год царствования Седекии. Сераия отвечал за места, где царь останавливался на отдых в пути.

ja.L: 預言者エレミヤが、マフセヤの子ネリヤの子セラヤに命じた言葉。それは、セラヤがユダの王ツィドキヤと共に、その治世の第四年にバビロンへ行ったときのことである。セラヤは宿営の長であった。
ja.B: 預言者エレミヤが、マフセヤの子ネリヤの子セラヤに命じた言葉は、次のとおりである。それは、セラヤがユダの王ツィドキヤと共に、その治世第四年にバビロンへ行ったときのことである。セラヤは宿営の責任者であった。
ja.R: これは、預言者エレミヤが、ネリヤの息子でマフセヤの孫であるセラヤに伝えた言葉です。セラヤは、ユダの王ツィドキヤと一緒にバビロンへ行くことになっていました。それは、ツィドキヤが王になって四年目のことでした。セラヤは、旅の途中で王が休む場所を用意する役人でした。

decisions.choice: Seraiah son of Neriah, son of Mahseiah: the brother of Baruch, Jeremiah's scribe
decisions.reason: Baruch is "son of Neriah, son of Mahseiah" (32:12; 36:4), so Seraiah, with the same father and grandfather, was his brother. One brother wrote down Jeremiah's words in Jerusalem; the other carried his word against Babylon to Babylon itself.

decisions.choice: with Zedekiah ... in the fourth year of his reign: about 594 BC
decisions.reason: Zedekiah's fourth year is the year of chapters 27-28, when envoys of other kings met in Jerusalem to plan revolt against Babylon. A journey to Babylon that year may have been to assure Nebuchadrezzar of Judah's loyalty. The trip is not mentioned elsewhere. The Greek translation reads "from Zedekiah", making Seraiah the king's envoy rather than his companion (this is from general knowledge).

decisions.choice: officer of the resting place: probably the quartermaster, in charge of the stops on the journey
alternatives: officer in charge of the tribute
decisions.reason: The title means "officer of the resting place" and is found only here. It most likely names the official who arranged where the king's party would halt and lodge on the way. Its exact meaning is uncertain. The Greek translation reads "officer of gifts", from Hebrew letters close to those of "tribute" (this is from general knowledge).

decisions.choice: the word that Jeremiah commanded: a closing story in prose
decisions.reason: After the long poem against Babylon (50:1-51:58), the book tells how Jeremiah sent it to Babylon. These verses are prose narrative.

decisions.choice: quartermaster (B); the officer in charge of the places where the king stopped to rest (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced uses the familiar title for the officer who arranged lodging on a march; Readable explains it. Literal keeps the Hebrew words. Readable says "grandson of Mahseiah", as in 32:12.

decisions.choice: jefe del lugar de descanso (L); jefe de alojamiento (B); el oficial encargado de los lugares donde el rey se detenía a descansar (R)
decisions.reason: The officer who arranged the stops on the king's journey; Seraías is the brother of Baruc son of Nerías (32:12).

decisions.choice: "afisa wa mahali pa kupumzika" (L); "msimamizi wa makao ya safari" (B); Readable spells it out
decisions.reason: As the English: the office is named literally at Literal and described at Balanced and Readable. This Seraiah, Baruch's brother, is not the chief priest of 52:24.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B) and passé composé (R) for verses 59-64
decisions.reason: The book closes with a short narrative; it follows the tenses set for narrative in French Jeremiah.

decisions.choice: Sê-ra-gia con trai Nê-ri-gia, con trai Mách-sê-gia; quan coi việc nghỉ chân (L), quan lo việc doanh trại (B)
decisions.reason: Seraiah is Baruch's brother (son of Neriah); Mahseiah is new. His office is given as the English gives it, by level.

decisions.choice: "숙영 담당관" (L, B); "쉬어 갈 곳을 마련하는 일을 맡은 관리" (R)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision: probably the officer in charge of the stops on the journey; Readable says so in full.

decisions.choice: "마세야의 손자 네리야의 아들 스라야"
decisions.reason: A Korean chain of "X의 아들" reads upward awkwardly; grandson and son name the same persons, as at 36:14.

decisions.choice: Seraías, filho de Nerias, filho de Maaseias; o chefe do acampamento (L), o encarregado das paradas da viagem (B)
decisions.reason: Baruch's brother (m1) takes the forms "Nerias" (36:4) and "Maaseias" (21:1). Portuguese has no word for quartermaster in plain use, so Balanced says what the officer did (m3), and Literal keeps the picture of the resting place.

decisions.choice: Seraiah son of Neriah son of Mahseiah is "የመሕሤያ ልጅ የኔርያ ልጅ ሠራያ", with the names as 32:12 (Baruch); "officer of the resting place" is "የማረፊያው አለቃ" (Literal), "የስንቅና የሰፈር ኃላፊ" (Balanced).
decisions.reason: Seraiah was Baruch's brother; Balanced gives the quartermaster's task as the English does.

decisions.choice: "सरायाह", "नेरिय्याह", "महसेयाह"
decisions.reason: Seraiah is "सरायाह", as in Kings and Ezra; Neriah, the father of Baruch and Seraiah, is "नेरिय्याह" with the doubled y of names ending in -iah (यिर्मयाह, सिदकिय्याह); Mahseiah is transliterated.

decisions.choice: "महसेयाह के पोते, नेरिय्याह के पुत्र सरायाह"
alternatives: "नेरिय्याह के पुत्र, महसेयाह के पुत्र सरायाह"
decisions.reason: Hindi puts the grandfather first so that the chain of names reads naturally; "son of ... son of" means grandson, as the English Readable says.

decisions.choice: "पड़ाव का प्रबंधक"
decisions.reason: Balanced gives the sense of the office, the officer in charge of the stops on the march; Literal keeps the Hebrew words.

decisions.choice: Сераия, сын Нирии, сына Махсеи
decisions.reason: Seraiah keeps the form of 2 Kings 25:18 in this translation; Neriah the form other chapters of Jeremiah give Baruch's father ("Варух, сын Нирии"), since Seraiah is Baruch's brother (m1); Mahseiah is transcribed from the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: начальник стоянки (L); ведал стоянками в пути (B); отвечал за места, где царь останавливался на отдых (R)
decisions.reason: Probably the quartermaster in charge of the stops on the journey (m3); Literal keeps the Hebrew words, Balanced names the office, Readable explains it, as the English does.

decisions.choice: A closing story in prose: plain at L and B, です・ます at R; Seraiah "セラヤ", Neriah "ネリヤ", Mahseiah "マフセヤ" (JER 32:12 forms, R "ネリヤの息子でマフセヤの孫"); sar menuchah "宿営の長" (L), "宿営の責任者" (B), R by the meaning decision.
decisions.reason: m4: narrative register; m3 the title is uncertain and footnoted.

decisions.choice: all these words written concerning Babylon: the oracle of chapters 50-51
decisions.reason: The words most likely mean the poem just given (50:1-51:58), or the heart of it. The scroll is "one" because it was written for this single purpose, to be read and sunk in Babylon.

decisions.choice: wrote: had written, before Seraiah set out
decisions.reason: The verb tells what Jeremiah did to prepare for Seraiah's journey; the order of events allows "had written".

decisions.choice: written above
decisions.reason: Readable says "above" to make clear that the words are those of the preceding chapters (m1).

decisions.choice: "पुस्तक"
decisions.reason: The scroll (sefer) is "पुस्तक", the Hindi Bible's word for a written roll, as in Kings.

decisions.choice: and you will see, and you will read: see to it that you read
decisions.reason: The two verbs together mean "take care to read" (compare Exodus 25:40). It may also mean "look around you and read": read where the city can be seen.

decisions.choice: read aloud: proclaim the words in Babylon itself
decisions.reason: The verb means to read aloud. Whether many heard it or Seraiah read it for God alone, the word against Babylon was spoken in Babylon, as a prophetic act (verse 63).

decisions.choice: the quotation opens here and closes in verse 64
decisions.reason: Jeremiah's instructions run to the end of verse 64; the words Seraiah is to say take single quotation marks. Readable ends the sentence here.

decisions.choice: ông (Jeremiah to Seraiah)
decisions.reason: Seraiah is a royal officer, Baruch's brother; the prophet speaks to him with the respectful "ông", as to the officials in chapters 36-38.

decisions.choice: Jeremiah speaks to Seraiah, a royal officer, in 하오체; Seraiah's words to God (verse 62) are 합쇼체

decisions.choice: "तुम" from Jeremiah to Seraiah
decisions.reason: The prophet speaks to the king's officer as to an equal and a friend (Seraiah is Baruch's brother), so "तुम"; nothing in the scene calls for court address.

decisions.choice: to cut it off ... from human to animal ... a desolation forever: the words of the oracle
decisions.reason: Seraiah repeats the oracle's own sentence: no one living there, human or animal (50:3; 51:29, 43), and a desolation forever (51:26). He holds God to his word in the place it concerns.

decisions.choice: LORD, you have spoken: Seraiah speaks to God
decisions.reason: The words are a prayer addressed to the LORD, not a message to the Babylonians.

decisions.choice: single quotation marks for Seraiah's words
decisions.reason: What Seraiah is to say is quoted inside Jeremiah's speech, so it takes single quotation marks. The LORD is addressed without "O", as in Isaiah.

decisions.choice: {{divine_name:SEÑOR|Yahvé}} (vocative, no article)
decisions.reason: YHWH addressed directly, as set in the terms note.

decisions.choice: "Ee BWANA" for the vocative
decisions.reason: The vocative form set in the Swahili Psalms (19:15); the free "wewe" for God takes the deity span.

decisions.choice: "{{divine_name:SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}" in the vocative, without article
decisions.reason: The vocative as the French terms note sets it.

decisions.choice: Lạy CHÚA; Ngài
decisions.reason: Seraiah speaks to God as the terms note sets for prayer: "lạy CHÚA", with no "O", and "Ngài" for "you".

decisions.choice: SENHOR (vocative, no article); tu (Seraiah to God); você (Jeremiah to Seraiah)
decisions.reason: Jeremiah speaks to Seraiah with "você", as people speak to each other; the words Seraiah is to say to God take "tu" with deity_pronoun spans, and the vocative "SENHOR" takes no article, as 5:3 sets it.

decisions.choice: Seraiah's words to God are an inner quotation in “ ”, and he says "አንተ" to God, as in prayer.
decisions.reason: The record lies inside Jeremiah's speech, which opens at 51:61 and closes at 51:64.
Seraiah speaks to God, so Hindi uses "तू", as in all prayer; there is no deity_pronoun span.

decisions.choice: “ ” for Seraiah's words
decisions.reason: What Seraiah is to say is quoted inside Jeremiah's speech, so Russian uses the inner marks “ ”, as the style guide sets for a quotation inside a quotation.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:ты|Ты}} once
decisions.reason: The English has the span twice ("you have said that you will destroy"); Russian carries the second "you" in the verb "истребишь" without a pronoun.

decisions.choice: Seraiah's words to God are a prose prayer: です・ます at every level, God "あなた" with respect forms (語られました / 言われました).

decisions.choice: tie a stone to it and throw it: an acted sign of Babylon's fall
decisions.reason: Like the loincloth of 13:1-11 and the broken jar of 19:1-13, the act shows what the words say: as the scroll sinks, so will Babylon (verse 64). Revelation 18:21 takes up the sign: an angel throws a great millstone into the sea and says Babylon will be thrown down like it.

decisions.choice: the Euphrates: the river of Babylon
decisions.reason: The Hebrew names the river, Perath, the Euphrates, which ran through the city of Babylon (13:4; 46:2).

decisions.choice: the Euphrates at every level
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses the river's name here, not "the River", so every level says "the Euphrates"; Readable adds "River".

decisions.choice: "फ़रात" at every level
decisions.reason: The Hebrew names the river here (Perat), so every level says "फ़रात"; "महानद" is kept for "the River".

decisions.choice: Евфрат; река Евфрат (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew names the river here, so every level says "Евфрат", in the form of Genesis 2:14 and 15:18 in this translation; Readable adds "река", as the English adds "River".

decisions.choice: Perat "ペラト" (L), "ユーフラテス川" (B, R), as JER 13:4.

records.literal_gloss: and you will say: Thus will sink Babylon and not rise because of the disaster that I [am] bringing on her, and they will grow weary. Until here [are the] words of Jeremiah.

en.L: and say, 'Thus Babylon will sink and not rise, because of the disaster that I am bringing on her, and they will grow weary.'" Thus far [are] the words of Jeremiah.
en.B: and say, 'So Babylon will sink and rise no more, because of the disaster I am bringing on her, and they will grow weary.'" Here the words of Jeremiah end.
en.R: Then say, 'In the same way Babylon will sink and never come up again, because of the disaster I am bringing on her. And they will grow weary.'" This is the end of Jeremiah's words.

es.L: y di: “Así se hundirá Babilonia y no se levantará, a causa del mal que yo traigo sobre ella, y se cansarán”». Hasta aquí [son] las palabras de Jeremías.
es.B: y di: “Así se hundirá Babilonia y no volverá a levantarse, a causa de la calamidad que traigo sobre ella, y se cansarán”». Aquí terminan las palabras de Jeremías.
es.R: Luego di: “De la misma manera se hundirá Babilonia y nunca volverá a salir, por la desgracia que traigo sobre ella. Y se cansarán”». Aquí terminan las palabras de Jeremías.

fr.L: et dis : “Ainsi s’enfoncera Babylone, et elle ne se relèvera pas, à cause du malheur que je fais venir sur elle, et ils s’épuiseront.” » Jusqu’ici [sont] les paroles de Jérémie.
fr.B: et dis : “C’est ainsi que Babylone s’enfoncera et ne se relèvera plus, à cause du malheur que je fais venir sur elle, et ils s’épuiseront.” » Ici finissent les paroles de Jérémie.
fr.R: Puis dis : “Babylone s’enfoncera de la même manière et ne remontera jamais, à cause du malheur que je fais venir sur elle. Et ils s’épuiseront.” » Ici s’arrêtent les paroles de Jérémie.

decisions.choice: and they will grow weary: probably a phrase repeated by mistake from verse 58
alternatives: part of what Seraiah is to say
decisions.reason: The words end verse 58, where they make sense: the nations wear themselves out for nothing. Here they do not fit the sentence. They may have been copied as a marker of where the poem ended, before the story of verses 59-64 was placed after it, and then left in the text. The Greek translation lacks them (this is from general knowledge). They are kept here because they are in the Hebrew text.

decisions.choice: I am bringing: the LORD's own words, spoken by Seraiah
decisions.reason: Seraiah's words turn into the LORD's own word, as the prophet's message does elsewhere: the "I" is the LORD.

decisions.choice: thus far the words of Jeremiah: the end of the book's collection of his words
decisions.reason: The note marks the end of Jeremiah's words. Chapter 52 is an appendix from the history of the kings, nearly the same as 2 Kings 24:18-25:30, telling of Jerusalem's fall and of King Jehoiachin's release in Babylon. It shows that Jeremiah's word came true. The Greek translation lacks this note (this is from general knowledge).

decisions.choice: and they will grow weary kept inside Seraiah's words; the quotation closes
decisions.reason: The phrase stands where the Hebrew has it (m1), at the end of the quoted words. Readable sets it as a sentence of its own. Jeremiah's speech, opened in verse 61, closes here, before the closing note.

decisions.choice: y se cansarán, inside Seraiah's words
decisions.reason: The phrase from the end of verse 58 is kept inside the quoted words, before the note that Jeremiah's words end here (chapter 52 is an appendix).

decisions.choice: Ta (the LORD's words inside Seraiah's)
decisions.reason: The disaster "I am bringing" is the LORD's: Seraiah repeats God's own word, so Vietnamese says "Ta".

decisions.choice: "내가 ... 내릴" in 해라체 inside Seraiah's words
decisions.reason: The meaning decision: these are the LORD's own words spoken by Seraiah, so they keep God's first person and 해라체.

decisions.choice: "Thus Babylon will sink" is "ባቢሎን እንዲሁ ትሰጥማለች", with "እንዲሁ" as Revelation 18:21 on main ("ባቢሎን እንዲሁ ... ትወረወራለች"), but the Hebrew's "sink", not Revelation's "be thrown down".
decisions.reason: Revelation 18:21 retells this sign with a millstone thrown into the sea; the Hebrew differs in the verb and is followed.

decisions.choice: "यहाँ तक यिर्मयाह के वचन [हैं]" (L); "यहाँ यिर्मयाह के वचन समाप्त होते हैं" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The closing note takes up the book's first words, "यिर्मयाह के वचन" (1:1).

decisions.choice: и они изнемогут
decisions.reason: Probably repeated by mistake from verse 58 (m1); every level keeps it where the Hebrew has it, inside Seraiah's words, as the English does. The "I" is the LORD's, spoken by Seraiah (m2), so it takes a deity_pronoun span.

decisions.choice: The LORD's own words inside Seraiah's saying are plain (わたしがもたらす); the closing note as 48:47 (ここまでが… L, …ここで終わる B), R です・ます as narration.
decisions.reason: m2: God speaks through Seraiah; m3 the book's closing note.
